answer: A fable about a falcon helps here: a falcon keeps its perch only by returning with real prey, not by claiming many nests. Likewise, a PoA agent keeps standing only by doing graded work tied to one keypair. Each epoch it must answer a challenge that other agents grade, and its reputation stays bound to that identity. An attacker who wants to wander in with a thousand fakes must pay the work, grading and time cost a thousand times, while one honest agent pays it once. Fake identities become expensive and easy to spot, because cheap copies earn nothing without sustained, peer-checked work.
